summary: This component covers activity from July 1, 2019, through June 30, 2020, and was collected in the 2020-21 reporting cycle. It reports institution-level 12-month enrollment and instructional activity for eligible IPEDS institutions, including undergraduate and graduate populations. Enrollment is measured as an unduplicated annual headcount, while instructional activity is reported as credit and/or contact hours; the component has no even- or odd-year-only collection rule.

The Completions survey reports awards and related program offerings from IPEDS-reporting postsecondary institutions for the academic year July 1, 2019, through June 30, 2020. Its universe is institutions with degree or certificate completions or programs to report; observations are institution-level, with some tables further broken out by program, award level, or student characteristics. Counts cover awards conferred during the reporting period rather than enrollment at a point in time.

The Fall Enrollment survey captures enrollment at eligible postsecondary institutions as of October 15 or the institution’s official fall reporting date for traditional academic calendars, or for students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31 for other calendar systems. The unit of observation is the institution, with tables adding demographic, academic, or enrollment-status dimensions to institution-level records. The survey covers institutions reporting fall enrollment; some measures have narrower eligibility or calendar-system restrictions identified in the individual table summaries.

The Finance component is reported in the 2020–21 collection cycle for institutional fiscal years ending between July 1, 2019, and June 30, 2020. Its unit of observation is the postsecondary institution, and its universe is Title IV-eligible institutions reporting institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, liabilities, and related finance measures under the applicable accounting framework. Public institutions use the GASB or FASB form as appropriate, while private institutions use the FASB forms; detailed expenditure categories discontinued beginning in fiscal year 2016 are not available.

The 2020 Graduation Rates collection was reported during the winter 2020–21 collection period and records student status as of August 31, 2020. It contains institution-level outcome counts for cohorts of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at eligible degree-granting Title IV institutions, with cohorts and normal-time thresholds varying by institution type and table. Outcomes are reported for students who completed, transferred, or remained in the cohort as applicable; the tables use separate cohorts for four-year, two-year, and less-than-two-year institutions.

Human Resources tables cover institution-level employees, with fall staffing counts generally reported for the payroll date of November 1 and salary measures for the academic year. Records are organized by UNITID and one or more staff classification dimensions; the tables differ in whether they cover all applicable institutions or only degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices. Counts and salary data are reported separately for staff populations and occupational groups, so eligibility and population restrictions must be checked at the table level.

Institutional Characteristics is collected in the fall for the 2020-21 academic year, with institutions reporting institution-level information for the IPEDS universe and Title IV participation making reporting mandatory for eligible Title IV institutions. The unit of observation is generally an IPEDS institution or administrative reporting unit identified by UNITID; active institutions, including parent/child reporting arrangements, may appear. The survey covers postsecondary institutions in the IPEDS universe, while some non-Title IV institutions may have voluntary or limited participation.

The Student Financial Aid component covers aid received during July 1, 2019–June 30, 2020 and is reported at the institution level by postsecondary institutions participating in federal Title IV aid programs. Student groups and aid categories are reported as institution-level counts and dollar amounts rather than individual-student records; eligibility and reporting requirements vary by table and population.
